cases.sentence: Как желанно твое жилище, о Господь Боже ___!
cases.explain: The genitive сил follows the noun Боже in the phrase 'Боже сил' (God of hosts/God of powers).

cases.sentence: Истомилась моя душа, желая быть во ___ храма Господа.
cases.explain: The preposition во (in) with prepositional case indicates location in the courts.

cases.sentence: Даже воробей находит себе дом и ласточка ___.
cases.explain: The verb находит (finds) takes the accusative case for its direct object гнездо.
The preposition в (in) with prepositional requires тебе.

cases.sentence: Проходя долину плача, они открывают в ней ___.
cases.explain: The verb открывают (find/discover) requires the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Один день во дворах твоих лучше тысячи вне его ___.
cases.explain: The genitive стен shows possession: 'outside its walls'.

cases.sentence: Господь Бог солнце ищит, и награда Господа — благодать и ___.
cases.explain: Слава is part of a nominative predicate after the dash parallel to благодать.

cases.sentence: О Господь сил! Блажен человек, уповающий на ___!
cases.explain: The verb уповающий (trusting) takes the preposition на with accusative Тебя.

reading.ru: Как желанно твое жилище, о Господь Бог сил!
reading.question: What does the psalmist find desirable?
options: God's dwelling place is lovely and desirable
reading.correct: God's dwelling place is lovely and desirable
reading.explain: The text states 'Как желанно твое жилище, о Господь Бог сил!' (How lovely is Your dwelling place, O Lord God of hosts!).

reading.ru: Истомилась моя душа, желая быть во дворах храма Господа.
reading.question: What does the psalmist's soul long for?
options: To be in the courts of the Lord's temple
To rest in a comfortable bed
To feast at a great banquet
reading.correct: To be in the courts of the Lord's temple
reading.explain: The text explicitly states 'Истомилась моя душа, желая быть во дворах храма Господа' (My soul longs to be in the courts of the Lord's temple).

reading.ru: Благословен человек, сила которого в тебе, в чьем сердце есть желание отправиться в Иерусалим.
reading.question: Who is described as blessed?
options: The person whose strength is in God and whose heart desires to go to Jerusalem
The person who has great military power
The person who owns vast territories
The person who has many servants
reading.correct: The person whose strength is in God and whose heart desires to go to Jerusalem
reading.explain: The psalm states 'Благословен человек, сила которого в тебе, в чьем сердце есть желание отправиться в Иерусалим' (Blessed is the one whose strength is in You, in whose heart are the highways to Zion).

reading.ru: Один день во дворах твоих лучше тысячи вне его стен, лучше быть у порога дома Божьего.
reading.question: What comparison does the psalmist make about dwelling in God's house?
options: One day in Your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere, better to be at the threshold of God's house
A thousand days outside are better than one day inside
Days outside the temple are more blessed
reading.correct: One day in Your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere, better to be at the threshold of God's house
reading.explain: The verse clearly states 'Один день во дворах твоих лучше тысячи вне его стен, лучше быть у порога дома Божьего' (One day in Your courts is better than a thousand outside, I would rather be a doorkeeper in God's house).

reading.ru: Тех, кто ходит непорочно, он не лишает благ.
reading.question: What does God not deprive those who walk blamelessly of?
options: God does not withhold good things from those who walk blamelessly
God takes away benefits from the righteous
God ignores those who obey him
reading.correct: God does not withhold good things from those who walk blamelessly
reading.explain: The text states 'Тех, кто ходит непорочно, он не лишает благ' (He will not withhold good things from those who walk blamelessly).

reading.ru: Сердце мое и плоть поют Богу живому.
reading.question: Who or what does the psalmist's heart and body sing to?
reading.explain: The psalmist declares 'Сердце мое и плоть поют Богу живому' (My heart and my being cry out in praise to the living God).
